thread:
maria: quick question — we have a secret that Terraform creates in another repo (myteam-shared-secrets). chart currently expects .Values.secrets.name. should Helm try to error if missing or render a conditional secretRef?

leo: i'd prefer a conditional in the chart so deploys don't blow up. we can default to empty env and log a warning. example pattern: 

maria: yep can you paste a snippet?

leo: sure — values.yaml: 
```yaml
secrets:
  useExternal: true
  name: myteam-shared-secrets
  key: api_key
```
and in the deployment template: 
```yaml
- name: API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: {{- if .Values.secrets.useExternal }}{{ .Values.secrets.name | quote }}{{- else }}""{{- end }}
      key: {{ .Values.secrets.key | default "api_key" | quote }}
```

raj: small caveat — putting an empty name into secretKeyRef is invalid k8s. better to conditionalize the whole env var entry or fallback to value: "". e.g.: 
```yaml
{{- if .Values.secrets.useExternal }}
- name: API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: {{ .Values.secrets.name | quote }}
      key: {{ .Values.secrets.key | quote }}
{{- else }}
- name: API_KEY
  value: ""
{{- end }}
```

alex: another option is to detect runtime presence of the Secret with lookup (Helm template function). that lets the chart adapt even if values lie. something like: 
```gotmpl
{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace .Values.secrets.name }}
{{- if $s }}
- name: API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: {{ .Values.secrets.name | quote }}
      key: {{ .Values.secrets.key | quote }}
{{- else }}
- name: API_KEY
  value: ""
{{- end }}
```

maria: lookup sounds nice — does it work in helm template during CI (helm lint / template)?

leo: lookup only works when you run against a cluster (helm template doesn't call cluster). so in CI you'd still want a values-driven fallback or a test harness to create a fake secret.

raj: for required secrets we sometimes use the required function so deploys fail fast with a clear message: 
```gotmpl
{{- $name := required "secrets.name is required in production" .Values.secrets.name }}
```
but that's opinionated — not great for charts that support both self-managed and external secrets.

maria: got it. what about templating secret names that include release name? our terraform creates a cluster-wide secret with a fixed name, but some envs use release-specific secrets. any recommended values layout?

alex: I'd expose both patterns in values: 
```yaml
secrets:
  type: external # options: external, release
  name: "shared-creds"
  releasePrefix: true
  key: api_key
```
and template: 
```gotmpl
{{- if eq .Values.secrets.type "release" }}
  {{- $secretName := printf "%s-%s" .Release.Name .Values.secrets.name }}
{{- else }}
  {{- $secretName := .Values.secrets.name }}
{{- end }}
```
but remember to actually use the scoped variable (avoid leaving it in an inner scope).

maria: nice. last nit — we're passing secret names through values and sometimes those values contain template snippets (e.g., "{{ .Release.Namespace }}-foo"). do we need tpl?

leo: yes use tpl when you want Helm to evaluate a value as a template with the chart context. example: 
```gotmpl
name: {{ tpl .Values.secrets.name . | quote }}
```
That lets values contain templated strings.

helm-bot: reminder — if you rely on tpl and lookup, chart behavior differs between helm install (server-side rendering) and helm template (client-side). CI that runs `helm template` will not resolve cluster lookups. :information_source:

maria: great; plan is: default to values-driven conditional, add lookup as optional runtime enhancement, and document that CI should set useExternal=false or provide test secret. i'll update the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:

leo: ping me when PR is up, i'll do a quick lint + values test.

raj: also add a short note in README about expected Terraform secret ownership and upgrade steps.

maria: will do — thanks!
